coverage.note: Albuquerque chapter page read. Santa Fe DSA site (dsasantafe.org) did not resolve; San Juan County is an organizing committee and Paso del Norte has no readable site, so those are unchecked.

Maine DSA is the only Maine chapter. Its endorsements page lists only 2024 to 2026 items (none for the legislature before 2026). 2022 and earlier-cycle legislative and governor endorsements unchecked: electoral.dsausa.org past-endorsements returned 403.

No 2023 to 2026 Virginia governor or General Assembly endorsement found on these chapter pages. The Metro DC DSA 2026 page lists Virginia constitutional amendments only; its only Virginia House of Delegates statement is a 2021 endorsement (out of scope). Social media and image-only posts were not audited; Shenandoah Valley is an organizing committee and was not checked.

Omaha DSA 2026 voter guide says the chapter is not doing endorsements. Lincoln DSA homepage has no endorsement page. National electoral.dsausa.org endorsement database not readable (Airtable); 2022 and 2024 chapter endorsements unverified.

Unchecked: dedsa.org and the DSA national Airtable/past-endorsements pages render no text, so the full 2022 to 2026 endorsement list could not be read. Entries come from the chapter Bluesky feed (205 items back to 2023-11-05) plus a saved Airtable extract for Wilson-Anton 2024. No 2022 or 2026 primary-stage DSA endorsements found. Lambert and Pinkney are named as endorsed with no election, so they are in gaps, not entries.
Champions page state filter has no NM; past-endorsement archive page 1 has no NM item. Archive pagination and a chapter list were not walked; /groups/ 404 per saved notes.

National site: 2023 general guide and recap (7 names), 2025 primary post (Cole). Site search for virginia, delegate and house of delegates found nothing else in scope. Our Revolution Northern Virginia was not checked beyond a web search that found no slate.
No Nebraska text on the first page of either; past-endorsement archive pagination and chapter pages not exhausted; /groups/ 404 per earlier notes.

The ME category holds only 2026 items (three legislative; Dunlap ME-02 and Jackson US Senate are out of scope), so no 2022 or 2024 Maine entries and no governor entry were found. Local Our Revolution groups in Maine were not enumerated.

Unchecked: Delaware chapter pages (saved evidence: /groups/ returns 404, no chapter page found) and a per-cycle 2022 to 2026 endorsement archive. Read: https://ourrevolution.com/our-champions/ and the past-endorsement category page; neither lists Delaware.

2022, 2024 and 2026 endorsement pages and the 2022 champions list show no Maine state-office entries (only Troy Jackson, US Senate 2026, out of scope). The 2020 champion Thomas Harnett (HD83) is out of scope and a champions list alone is not an endorsement. Web search found no PCCC governor endorsement.
2026 endorsements page has no NM state office. 2022 and 2024 endorsement pages and champions lists were not re-fetched; champions lists are not endorsements.
No Nebraska text on 2022 and 2024 pages. 2026 page names only Dan Osborn (U.S. Senate, out of scope).

The 2023 champions page lists 25 Virginia legislative names but is a champions list, not an endorsement statement, so none are entered. One 2025 endorsement (Jessica Anderson) rests on an ActBlue fundraiser page that does not name its entity. Blue Voter Guide returned a bot challenge, and no PCCC-hosted 2025 Virginia list was found.

Unchecked: the 2024 champions page returned no text, so 2024 could not be checked. Read: 2022 champions list (Kyra Hoffner, SD-14, a champions list only, not an endorsement) and the 2026 endorsements page (no Delaware row).
2022, 2023, 2025 pages list no NM state-legislative cards; 2024 lists Nava and Anaya; 2026 list page shows none but the profile for Jungmann exists. 2020 Linda Serrato (HD45) is out of scope.

Directory cards for 2023 (26 state legislative) and 2025 (14). The 2022, 2024 and 2026 directories list Virginia local candidates only. The 2021 cohort is out of scope (those terms ended in January 2024). RFS release-only candidacies noted in earlier repo reviews were not reconciled.

Directory year pages read for DE state-legislative cards. 2020 cards (Pinkney, McBride, Gay, Wilson-Anton) out of scope. Press-release-only candidacies not re-reconciled; the saved comparison shows only Rae Krantz (HD6, 2026-06-02 release) as a DE state-legislative release row. Governor not endorsed by RFS.

Static directory pages show five Maine cards but may be partial (saved notes: RFS 2026 count unreconciled, name variants and release-only candidacies unreviewed). RFS does not endorse governors. Special elections not checked.

Ten state legislature cards from saved directory extraction (research_notes/State endorsement gap review/rfs_pccc_directory_cards.tsv), each card re-fetched. Cards for school boards, city councils and other non-legislative offices skipped. No 2023 or 2025 state-level cards.
Endorsements archive first page and hubs page show no NM item. Older archive pages were not paged through.
No Nebraska text on the endorsements or hubs pages. Historical endorsement archives not separately checked.

Only Delaware hub is Sunrise Newark (University of Delaware microsite on Wix). Endorsement pages render almost no text; saved evidence says the 2020 archive is image-only and no 2022 to 2026 source was verified.

Only Virginia endorsement found is the 2021-03-22 release for Jennifer Carroll Foy (governor, 2021 primary) and Sam Rasoul (lieutenant governor); the 2021 election is outside scope because its term ended in January 2026. Local hubs (for example Sunrise Tidewater) were not audited.

Saved notes show one Maine hub (Franklin County) with only an Instagram presence, which is inaccessible. No national Sunrise endorsement list was checked for any cycle, nor was any governor endorsement.

2022 first-round slate and 2026 candidate list captured. No 2024 WFP NM post found on workingfamilies.org; 2024 and 2022 later rounds are open (see gaps). 2022 and 2026 governor: only Haaland 2026 found.

Current national candidates page lists Maine only for Troy Jackson (US Senate, out of scope); /state/maine/ is 404. No 2022 or 2024 archive and no 2022 or 2026 governor endorsement page was found, so those cycles are unchecked. Web search found only Platner (US Senate, 2026) and 2018 governor endorsements.
National candidates page Nebraska section lists only county DA and sheriff candidates (out of scope). State page /state/nebraska/ returns 404. No chapter page found.

Unchecked: the full 2022 WFP slate (only candidates named in a Sept 2022 recap and a later summary were found), and any WFP endorsements in the 2025-02-15 SD1 and SD5 special elections. Read: state page, candidates page (incl. rows behind View More), 2022 recap, 2024 slate, 2026 slate release. 2020 endorsements skipped as out of scope.

workingfamilies.org has no Virginia state page (404) and no Virginia legislative posts in its post sitemap. The 2025 slate (8 legislative candidates plus a lieutenant governor pick, excluded) comes from press coverage only. Virginia Mercury, RVA Magazine and Blue Voter Guide were not fetchable by script (403), so the full WFP Virginia list and any 2023 slate are unverified.

2022 and 2024 rows come from DSA's national past-endorsements grid (Denver chapter only; saved evidence). Denver DSA's 2026 guides endorse only a federal candidate and merely recommend state legislators. NoCo DSA endorses Yara Zokaie (HD52) in 2026. COS DSA's Nov 2026 guide covers ballot measures only. Boulder DSA and Mesa County DSA pages showed no endorsement text or no website. Denver and NoCo pages for 2022 and 2024 were not found on the sites. Blocked because Boulder and Mesa County pages gave no endorsement text, and Denver/NoCo pages for 2022 and 2024 were not found.

Atlanta DSA endorses Gabriel Sanchez (2024, 2026) and Mathewos Samson (2026); the 2024 row comes from the national Airtable grid, saved. Atlanta DSA's 2026 voter guide covers statewide races only. Athens Area and Savannah pages describe a process but list no candidates. Not checked: Middle Georgia, West Georgia, Augusta CSRA, and Northwest Georgia (organizing committee, no site) chapter feeds; older Atlanta DSA endorsement pages for 2022.

Found: East Bay DSA 2024 (Beckles), and two 2022 rows from the national Airtable (no chapter page). No 2026 chapter endorsements of legislators found on the pages that render text. Not checked or unreadable: DSA-LA 2022/2024 pages (dsa-la.org returns a Cloudflare block), East Bay, Sacramento, Silicon Valley, Sonoma, Marin, Humboldt, Kern, Santa Cruz and other chapter archives, SLO and Santa Barbara and Inland Empire (JavaScript pages with no text), all chapter social feeds, DSA Long Beach 2022-2024 archives.

Metro Detroit 2026 slate and the national DSA tables read. Metro Detroit 2022 and 2024 pages are gone (2024 page returns 404), so a 2024 Dylan Wegela endorsement could not be checked. Huron Valley (Ann Arbor), Greater Lansing, Grand Rapids (voter guide gives recommendations, not endorsements), Southwest and Northwest Michigan show no state legislative endorsements. Saginaw Bay, Cadillac, Isabella County, Upper Peninsula not reviewed (social-only or organizing committees).

NYC-DSA 2024 and 2026 slates complete from press releases. 2022: only six of the 13-candidate NYC-DSA slate are sourced (four via Common Dreams, two via the saved national table); the other chapters (Mid-Hudson Valley, Lower Hudson Valley, Buffalo, Capital District, Ithaca, Long Island, Rochester, Syracuse, Troy, others) have saved site reviews but their endorsement pages were not re-read. NYC-DSA press archive has no 2022 endorsement releases.

Philadelphia DSA's 2022 rows come from the saved national Airtable extract (the page renders no text); the 2024 Cass Green row comes from a Reclaim Philadelphia report. Philly DSA's site now lists only 2027 city races. Pittsburgh DSA, Lehigh Valley DSA and NEPA DSA pages show no state-level endorsements. Not checked: Erie, Centre County and South Central PA chapters (no readable site or only social media), chapter social feeds, and Philadelphia/Pittsburgh endorsements from 2024 and 2026 that may live only on social media.

The saved national DSA tables hold one CT row (Justin Farmer SD17, 2020), out of scope. The chapter site shows no 2022-2026 state endorsements in the pages read. Chapter social feeds, branch pages and the 2026 gubernatorial analysis post were not checked for endorsements.
2026 House/Senate posts, 2024 post, and the past-MI category (only the 2024 post is there). No 2022 Michigan post found, no governor endorsement found. OR local chapters were not enumerated.

2026 and 2024 national-site pages read. No 2022 OR slate found. OR chapters (e.g. Wellstone Progressive Democrats/Our Revolution Sacramento, Our Revolution Long Beach) not checked. The 2024 guide covers Sacramento, Alameda, Contra Costa and Southern California slates only as written; other 2024 posts may exist.

2026 posts read (state races slate and Chambers). The PA category page shows only those two posts plus congressional ones. No 2022 or 2024 PA state-level post found, but the Our Revolution archive was not paged through. The undated 'Building Power in Pennsylvania' post lists Dylan Altemara (HD 39) with no election named, so it is in gaps. Blue Voter Guide's Our Revolution page returned 403. No governor endorsement found.

Colorado category page lists only 2026 posts (Gonzalez SoS, Kiros CO-01, Farrington RTD are out of scope). The 2024 slate is in a Revolution Report. No 2022 Colorado legislative endorsement found by site search. Local Our Revolution chapters were not enumerated. Blocked because chapter pages were not enumerated and 2022 was covered only by site search.

The Georgia category and the post sitemap show three Georgia posts: Romman (SD7), Samson (HD58) and Peter Hubbard (Public Service Commission, out of scope). No 2022 or 2024 Georgia legislative or governor endorsement found. Blocked because local Our Revolution groups were not enumerated and the site search is not an archive.

The NY category and a WordPress search list only 2026 legislative posts. Search results also name an Evan Menist SD-39 post and a standalone Adam Bojak AD-149 post, but neither URL could be fetched, so Menist is not listed. No 2022 or 2024 NY legislative or governor post found; Our Revolution chapters not checked.

The national site's CT category holds one post (Angie Parkinson, 2026). No 2022 or 2024 CT endorsement found there. Local Our Revolution chapters in Connecticut were not enumerated, so the status is blocked.

Endorsement pages for 2022, 2024 and 2026 list no Colorado governor or state-legislative candidate (2026 lists Jena Griswold and Melat Kiros, both out of scope). A 'champions' list and an undated ActBlue page naming a Colorado slate are not endorsements and name no election.

Only champions lists were reachable; they are not endorsements and name no CT state legislator. 2024 and 2026 state pages were not found on the issuer site.
